review_style.value: Reviewed contributors' Claude PRs, asking for changes in most; now asks for human audits
review_style.quote: After I asked to see benchmark runs to prove the gains weren’t just theoretical, they started including benchmark runs.

also.quote: Speaking from personal experience, reviewing the PRs from Claude&Rob was neither faster nor slower, easier nor harder, than what I’m used to pre-GenAI.
Interestingly, we got to the current epsilon-closure code in a sequence of reasonable-looking PRs that I reviewed, asking for changes in most.
This is mostly Claude-generated and does a whole bunch of different things in a mixed-up way and I don't understand it fully. Needs a careful human audit looking for ways to simplify.

harness.value: By hand: Quamina's CBOR flattener and its tests, no LLM
harness.quote: So once again, I’m not going to do it with LLMs.

also.quote: I’m doing this for fun. Writing high-performance tokenizers is fun!

rules_files.value: CONTRIBUTING.md GenAI section discouraging LLM-generated PRs
rules_files.quote: As of September 2026, Quamina discourages PRs substantially generated by an LLM.

signature.caption: Claude scans still welcome
signature.why: Our pick: Claude-written code is out, but Claude security findings stay welcome, so Quamina's users don't pay for a dislike of the source.
signature.quote: There’s an exception to my new policy: Vulnerability reports. I think it’d be irresponsible to ignore them and penalize Quamina’s users because I don’t like the source.

archetype.why: Merged Claude PRs for months, then stopped them, keeping only its vulnerability reports.

signature_quote.value: But in the big picture my reviewing was ineffective, because it ended with a large lump of code that I don’t understand or, at the end of the day, trust.
signature_quote.more: I wonder how typical that outcome is?

no_agent.value: Declines Claude for Quamina; writes it by hand
no_agent.quote: This would be a great job for Claude.” So far I’m ignoring it

also.quote: I’m not a GenAI expert, have never relied on it for any substantial piece of work.
I’ve never personally put clankers seriously to work and for now I’ll continue not to.
I am an LLM contra and don't use it myself, but Claude found an ugly data race in my Go code. Easy to reproduce once I read the report.
So anyhow, for now I’m not going to use any GenAI tools myself.
